key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset during activity - lifting, twisting, bending, or sudden movement. Often during heavy lifting, awkward positioning, or sudden movement. LOCATION: Lower back (lumbar), may radiate to buttocks or thighs. DURATION: Immediate pain that may worsen over first 24-48 hours. CHARACTER: SHARP initial pain, then THROBBING and ACHING. May have muscle spasms. AGGRAVATING: BENDING, lifting, twisting, sitting, standing, coughing, sneezing. RELIEVING: REST, heat, ice, NSAIDs, muscle relaxants. TIMING: Immediate pain, stiffness increases over 24-48 hours, then gradually improves over days to weeks. SEVERITY: 4-8/10, moderate to severe with movement. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: MUSCLE SPASMS, stiffness, difficulty moving, difficulty sitting or standing, may have referred pain to buttocks or thighs. KEY POSITIVES: Paraspinal muscle tenderness, muscle spasms, limited range of motion, positive straight leg raise test (if radicular symptoms). KEY NEGATIVES: No neurological deficits, no saddle anesthesia, no bowel/bladder dysfunction, no fever, no night pain.

includes.patient_friendly: all at once or very quickly

red_flags: Severe pain with neurological deficits - possible cauda equina syndrome, call 911
Saddle anesthesia or bowel/bladder dysfunction - cauda equina syndrome, call 911
Severe pain with fever - possible spinal infection, needs urgent evaluation
Severe pain with night pain - possible malignancy, needs urgent evaluation
Severe pain with weight loss - possible malignancy, needs urgent evaluation
